title: Let Us Be Thankful | Sri Daya Mata

# Let Us Be Thankful

### The Essence of Gratitude

Beloved ones, as we gather our hearts in the stillness of the Divine, we must contemplate one of the most potent keys to spiritual liberation: the virtue of thankfulness. In the teachings of our beloved Paramahansa Yogananda, we are reminded time and again that the heart which remains centered in gratitude is the heart that has already begun to dissolve the ego. When we are thankful, we are not merely expressing a polite social grace; we are tuning our consciousness to the very vibration of the Infinite, which is eternally giving.

### The Obstacle of Comparison

Why is it so difficult for the human heart to remain in a state of constant thanksgiving? It is because we fall into the trap of comparison. We look at the lives of others, or we look at our own perceived lacks, and we forget the Giver of all gifts. Yoganandaji taught us that every moment of existence is a miracle. To wake up, to breathe, to feel the pulsation of life within the veins—this is the greatest gift of all. Yet, we take it for granted. We focus on the thorns of life and forget the roses that bloom in the garden of our soul.

**Story • The Two Travelers**

Story: There were once two travelers walking along a dusty road toward a distant city. One traveler spent his entire journey complaining about the stones in his shoes, the heat of the sun, and the weight of his pack. He arrived at the city gate exhausted, bitter, and miserable. The second traveler, walking the same road, spent his time observing the beauty of the birds in the sky, the cooling breeze on his face, and the strength of his legs that allowed him to make the journey. He arrived at the same city gate, yet his heart was full of peace and his spirit was rejuvenated. The path did not change; only the perspective changed. Our lives are the same. We carry the same burdens, but it is our gratitude that lightens the load.

### Living in the Present

To be truly thankful, we must learn to live in the present. The past is a tomb of regrets, and the future is a phantom of anxieties. God dwells only in the 'now.' When you can look at your life, exactly as it is, and say, 'I am grateful,' a transformation occurs. You stop being a victim of circumstance and become a master of your own destiny. You realize that every challenge is but a hidden blessing, a sandpaper designed to polish the soul until it reflects the Divine Light.

### Conclusion

Let us, then, practice this. When you wake up, before your feet touch the floor, let your first thought be of thanks. Even in the face of sorrow, try to find one thing—even the smallest thing—for which you can offer your heart to the Divine. As you do this, you will find that the darkness begins to recede, and you are bathed in the ever-new joy of the Spirit.
